title: Sink ACK Coordination and Loss-Tolerance Model for Enterprise Webhook Integrations
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers using external SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, Managed SIEMs) and generic webhook sinks see intermittent loss, duplicate events, and difficulty reconciling audit timelines during failover or connector restarts. Existing webhook delivery retries and DLQ approaches surface at higher level but lack a coordinated acknowledgement model between redwood forwarder and third-party consumer that supports bounded replays and cost-predictable retention goals.

Goals:
- Define an ACK coordination protocol that reduces duplicate delivery while allowing consumer-side idempotence to remain simple.
- Provide loss-tolerance tiers (best-effort, at-least-once, bounded-replay-with-tokens) configurable per-tenant and per-sink.
- Ensure telemetry (metrics + traces) surfaced in Console for: sink health, recent replay windows, ack lag, and per-tenant loss incidents.
- Provide guidance and small SDK snippets for common partners (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, generic webhook receivers) to integrate with the protocol.

Constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Exactly-once semantics at scale are expensive; we prioritize deterministic, auditable reconciliation over high-cost, cross-system transactional guarantees.
- Protocol must be backward-compatible: existing customers using simple webhook retries should not be forced to migrate.
- Storage/retention for replay tokens must be cost-accounted and gated by dedicated capacity SLAs.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Sink ACK windows: messages are emitted with a per-sink sequence and a short-lived receipt token (opaque to the consumer). The forwarder maintains a sliding ack window (configurable size/time) and marks messages as resumable for replay within the window.
2) Idempotency & dedup: we ship a lightweight "replay-id" header and suggest consumer SDKs persist recent replay-ids for de-duplication. For heavier customers, recommend idempotency-key handshake using tenant-scoped keys.
3) Loss-tolerance tiers:
   - best-effort: current retry + backoff (legacy behavior), no replay tokens
   - at-least-once: retry + replay tokens valid for N minutes, higher retention cost
   - bounded-replay: deterministic replay token ledger with per-tenant window and audit traces; replay ledger purged per retention policy.
4) Backpressure & hinted-ack: when a sink signals overload (429/5xx with Retry-After), forwarder can switch to queued-only mode and expose a sink-health flag in Console; consumers can request a final checkpoint-by-token before temporary shutdown.
5) Observability: new metrics emitted: sink_ack_lag_seconds, sink_replay_request_count, sink_replay_success_rate, sink_dedup_rate, sink_heartbeat_latency. These map to per-route dashboards and alerts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implement ack window core in the forwarder with configuration flags per-sink and unit tests covering window slides, token expiry, and replay acceptance.
- Provide Splunk HEC and Datadog ingestion examples with de-dup guidance and a small reference consumer SDK in Go and Python (source links in PR).
- Console shows per-sink health indicators and a replay history table for last 7 days.
- Run integration smoke tests against partner staging endpoints that simulate overload and confirm bounded replay behavior.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (canary): implement ack window behind feature flag for 10% tenant sample, no default change for existing webhook sinks.
- Phase 1 (opt-in): SDK + documentation + allow tenants to opt-in to at-least-once tier. Monitor error budget and dedup metrics.
- Phase 2 (opt-out deprecation): after 10 weeks and zero critical incidents, make bounded-replay available as a paid option for Dedicated and Private customers.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/SEC-Audit-Sink-ACK-Model (internal)
- Reference PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/forwarder/pull/1482 (staging branch)
